The shipped ladder, player overrides, export and import, what the save holds, and building from source.

Presets and building

The shipped ladder

Presets/LadderV2.json is the book: every rung RimPLC ships with, in the ladder shape, with the sensor catalogue, the tags and the marks it needs. It loads with the mod and is not saved in the colony, so updating the mod updates the book in every save.

Editing a preset rung in the window (or with upsert_rung under its id) makes a player copy under the same id; the ladder uses the copy and the window's Revert drops it. Your own rungs, your switches, your advise/auto modes, your tag overrides, your marks, the instruction memory and the letters you have marked seen are saved with the colony.

Export and import

Export writes the ladder -- the book plus your layer -- to <RimWorld config folder>/RimPLC/exports/<name>.json, in the same shape as the preset plus an rimplc_state block with the memory.

Import reads one of those files (or any ladder in the shape) and shows the difference before anything changes:

MarkMeaning
+a rung the import adds
~a rung it changes
=a rung it leaves as is
!a rung it cannot take -- the reason is beside it

Apply merges it. A dry run through the command file ("dry_run": true) returns the same diff as text. Back up a colony before importing into it or switching game versions.

Clean notices

A rung's notice is text the game will show. Notices and messages from the external-assistant rungs pass a clean-word filter before they are shown; a line the filter rejects is not shown, and a rung whose notice would be rejected is refused at save time.

Building from source

dotnet build -c Release Source/RimPLC/RimPLC.csproj -p:RimWorldPath="C:/path/to/RimWorld"
dotnet build -c Release Source/RimPLC.BridgeTools/RimPLC.BridgeTools.csproj

RIMWORLD_PATH in the environment is also accepted. Both projects target .NET Framework 4.7.2 and C# 7.3, treat warnings as errors, and reference the game's Managed assemblies (and, for the companion, the installed RimBridgeServer.Sdk.dll) read-only with Private=false -- nothing of the game's is copied into the output. The core writes 1.7/Assemblies/RimPLC.dll; the companion writes BridgeTools/RimPLC.BridgeTools.dll. Neither build stages or launches the game.

The shipped preset is self-contained: nothing else is needed to build or run the mod. In the working repository it is generated from the playbook by a checker that enforces unique ids, numeric priorities, known keys, type-correct comparisons, a prompt for every rung and no priority ties; the window's editor applies the same rules to a rung you save.

Versions

The package declares RimWorld 1.6 and 1.7 and loads one 1.7/ folder for both. The compiler and API baseline is 1.6; a 1.7 running session has not yet been recorded as passing.

RimPLC. A development build; nothing here is a balance, performance or compatibility report.
